author: Widogeist
body:
Raid bosses get tankier as the fight progresses *in the current run*. If/when you die, their passive stats will reset to their default baseline, as if you just freshly summoned them.

You mention that your loadout is the same, passives are the same, etc.  The only other explanations I can think of are: 

* Maybe you're not receiving your origin town bonus (10% passive stats)? Have you recently traveled? You might just be getting the territory passive, but not OT passive (5% vs. 10%).

* Are you in a party? Maybe you lost your passive party bonus (lasts ~30 minutes) which gives an additional 10% passive stats.

* You mention using swordplay.  Swordplay can trigger temporary buffs on your character and temporary debuffs on the enemy.  Maybe your damage variance is because you have t.att+ and the enemy has t.def - in some rounds, and in other rounds the buffs/debuffs fall off.

author: dreambig5
body:
To start off I'll say I've read your other comments below. I'm guessing you're using like a warrior class and if you have summoner unlocked you might T9? I remember when I was using Nyx & High Taranis for quite a while. My mistake with my build was using Mirror (masterforged) for the crazy amount of Mana it gave but I didn't realize the importance of ward until then. It was a decent strategy for me from T4-T8 as I could constantly hit lightning strike III and similar attacks against monsters that were weak to it and do fair amount of damage.

After getting into raids, I realized I was having similar issues as you (I'd get few hits in and get killed). After ton of reading on others posts, I finally tried out Summoner, and was pleased to be able to finish most raids usually in one life if not two. There's various ways to play this class based on the specialization that one chooses. I went with Benefactor because of the stronger summons and change of summoning one turn quicker), but others might suggest something else like Charmer (so you can use Appease II and the sonatas to boost yourself while lowering enemy stats) or Chronomancer (which I haven't fully understood yet but can kind of freeze enemies in time so you have time to bring your 3 turn summons and 3 turn ward fixes like Mend Wall III safely). 

If you're sticking to your class if you share your loadout & skills that you're using, people might be able to help you better. 

Also pumpkinhead seems to be immune to lot (Burning, Bleeding, Frozen, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Blight, Blind, Asleep, Petrified, Rot and Def ↓, Def ↓↓, Res ↓↓, Res ↓). So no real weaknesses that can be targeted.

author: Anthonevil
body: Go on the discord and ask around for someone who has the NPC horus near them. Do the horus quest and it will unlock the summoner class for free for you. The summoner class is extremely OP from tier 7 to tier 10. Its going to be the easiest way to progress. The summoner is very rng dependant. Because if the raid boss targets you, you're probably going to die. But when you have all 5 of your summons spawned the chance of you getting targeted is very low. You'll go from only being able to get 6 hits in max before dying with your current class. To potentially killing the raid boss solo in one go with the summoner. Right now the summoner class is the way to go because it's so overpowered in the lower tiers. But the devs are about to release a patch to rework the different class lines leading up to tier 10. Hopefully this means they are going to boost the power of all the other classes to match the summoner. But we will see how that goes soon.
